description: Implement the parser that transforms tokens into an AST, and the compiler that generates bytecode from the AST. Includes the bytecode chunk representation and the code generator.
steps: Create /projects/sandbox/vek/src/chunk.h and /projects/sandbox/vek/src/chunk.c defining: the bytecode Chunk struct (uint8_t* code with count/capacity, Value* constants with count/capacity, int* lines for source mapping), OpCode enum with all ~60 opcodes from design doc section 12.4 (OP_NOP through OP_IMPORT), and functions chunk_init, chunk_write, chunk_add_constant, chunk_free.

Create /projects/sandbox/vek/src/compiler.h and /projects/sandbox/vek/src/compiler.c implementing a single-pass Pratt parser + compiler (no separate AST - compile directly to bytecode as we parse, similar to Lua/crafting interpreters approach). Key components: Compiler struct (enclosing compiler for nested functions, locals array with name/depth/is_captured, upvalues array, scope_depth, current Chunk), Parser struct (current/previous token, hadError, panicMode). Implement: expression parsing with Pratt precedence (prefix/infix rules for each token type), statement parsing (expression statements, variable declarations, assignments, if/elsif/else/end, while/end, until/end, for..in/end, loop do/end, fn declarations, return, break/next, begin/rescue/end, raise), variable resolution (locals, globals, upvalues for closures), and constant folding for simple cases.

Implement expression compilation: literals (nil, true, false, integers, floats, strings, symbols), unary operators (- ! ~), binary operators (+ - * / % == != < > <= >= && || & | ^ << >>), string interpolation (desugar to concat calls), list literals [a, b, c] -> OP_NEW_LIST, map literals {k: v} -> OP_NEW_MAP, field access (a.b -> OP_GET_FIELD), index access (a[b] -> OP_GET_INDEX), function calls (a(b, c) -> OP_CALL), method calls (a.b(c) -> OP_GET_FIELD + OP_CALL), safe navigation (?.), ternary (?:), range (.. ...).

Implement statement compilation: variable assignment (= with OP_SET_LOCAL/OP_SET_GLOBAL), if/elsif/else with jump patching (OP_JUMP_IF_FALSE + OP_JUMP), while loops with OP_JUMP back, for..in loops with OP_ITER_NEW/OP_ITER_NEXT, fn declarations creating ObjClosure with OP_CLOSURE and upvalue capture, return with OP_RETURN, break/next with jump tracking, begin/rescue with OP_PUSH_HANDLER/OP_POP_HANDLER.

Create /projects/sandbox/vek/src/debug.h and /projects/sandbox/vek/src/debug.c with a bytecode disassembler: disassemble_chunk prints each instruction with its offset, opcode name, and operands. Useful for development and the REPL.

Create /projects/sandbox/vek/tests/test_compiler.c testing: compiling simple expressions and verifying correct bytecode output, compiling variable declarations and assignments, compiling if/else control flow, compiling function declarations with closures, compiling for loops.
acceptance_criteria: Compiler successfully compiles arithmetic expressions to correct bytecode (OP_LOAD_CONST, OP_ADD, etc.)
Compiler handles variable declarations and produces OP_SET_LOCAL/OP_LOAD_GLOBAL correctly
Compiler handles if/elsif/else/end with correct jump offsets
Compiler handles while/for loops with correct back-jumps and break/next
Compiler handles fn declarations and produces OP_CLOSURE with upvalue capture
Compiler handles nested scopes and correctly resolves locals vs globals vs upvalues
Compiler reports errors for malformed syntax with line numbers
Disassembler prints readable bytecode for debugging
verification: Run 'make test' and confirm all compiler tests pass
findings: Implemented as a stack-based VM approach (not register-based) for Phase 1 simplicity, as noted in the briefing. Key decisions: (1) Variables in vek use implicit declaration via assignment - at global scope this emits DEFINE_GLOBAL, at local scope it creates a new local. (2) Newlines are consumed as insignificant after operators and brackets. (3) ObjFunction was updated to include a Chunk and name field. (4) The error message '[line 2] Error at end: Expected expression.' appears during the syntax_error test and is expected behavior (testing that bad syntax is caught). All 99 tests pass with zero warnings.
